chunks: They said: "O our Lord, we are really frightened lest he behave insolently with us or become violent."
ai.seo_question: What did Hud and his companion pray to God regarding their fear of tyranny?
ai.summary: Although the verse is often associated with Musa and Harun in broader tafsir, this specific narration attributes the plea to Prophet Hud and his companion facing the tyrant Qarun, highlighting the universal theme of divine protection against oppressive power. The phrase 'yafraṭ' (act recklessly) and 'yaṭghā' (exceed bounds) underscores the human vulnerability when confronting authority, a key concept in Shia exegesis regarding the Imams' struggles with Umayyad and Abbasid caliphs. This supplication serves as a model for believers seeking stability and guidance amidst political and social turmoil.
